!Sample_title = LentiGFP 1 [ATAC-seq]
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM6068778
!Sample_status = Public on Apr 14 2023
!Sample_submission_date = Apr 26 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Apr 15 2023
!Sample_type = SRA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = Primary rat Schwann cells
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Rattus norvegicus
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 10116
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = tissue: sciatic nerve
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell type: Schwann cells
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = treatment: infected/treated with control virus
!Sample_treatment_protocol_ch1 = Overexpression of the Egr2-AS-RNA (and the backbone virus control carrying GFP) was performed with a lentiviral construct at a concentration of 2UFC/cell, with polybrene at a 1:1500 concentration, for 48 hours. The virus generation was described in detail in previous work (Martinez-Moreno et al., 2017). The plasmid to generate the lentivirus was deposited to Addgene and is available to order (#177737).
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Cells were cultured in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 4 μM forskolin, 5 ng/ml heregulin-β1 and antibiotics, in surface modified 75cc Primaria flasks. Cells were fed every other day and passaged at 80% confluence.
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = genomic DNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = For each biological replicate, 100,000 cells were used to prepare ATACseq libraries following a modified protocol from Kaestner’s lab (Ackermann et al., 2016). After the transposition reaction, using the Nextera DNA Library Prep Kit, DNA was isolated using a MinElute Reaction Cleanup Kit. To make the libraries, we used the NEBNext High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix. Primers (universal and indexing) used are listed in Table 1. For multiplexing, we used the same universal primers for every sample, and every sample had their unique indexing primer. Quality control (QC) of the libraries was performed before sequencing using KAPA Library Quantification Kit for Illumina Platforms.
!Sample_description = ATAC DNA
!Sample_data_processing = FASTQ files of sequencing reads for each sample provided by GENEWIZ were aligned to the RGSC6.0/rn6 Rattus norvegicus reference genome (https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/rn6/bigZips/rn6.fa.gz) using Bowtie2 (http://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/bowtie2/index.shtml). Reads with a mapping quality of 30 or better were retained for analysis. Duplicate reads were remove with Picard (https://github.com/broadinstitute/picard).
!Sample_data_processing = ATAC peaks were detected with MACS2 (https://pypi.org/project/MACS2/). Peaks with a -log10qvalue at peak summit of 5 or greater were retained for further analysis.
!Sample_data_processing = Gene promoters were defined as the regions from -1500 to +500 nucleotides with respect to the annotated Transcription Start Sites in RefSeq, as extracted from the refGene.txt file (http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/rn6/database/refGene.txt.gz).
!Sample_data_processing = ATAC peaks mapping to promoters were detected with the intersectBed routine of bedtools (https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), using the peaks coordinates and the promoter coordinates as inputs.
!Sample_data_processing = ATAC read mapping to peaks or promoter regions were counted and summarized with featureCounts (https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btt656).
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: Rn6 (Rnor_6.0)
!Sample_data_processing = Supplementary files format and content: narrowPeak files
!Sample_platform_id = GPL18694
!Sample_contact_name = Jorge,Eduardo,Fajardo
!Sample_contact_email = eduardo@fiserlab.org
!Sample_contact_department = Systems and Computational Biology
!Sample_contact_institute = Albert Einstein College of Medicine
!Sample_contact_address = 1300 Morris Park Avenue
!Sample_contact_city = Bronx
!Sample_contact_state = NY
!Sample_contact_zip/postal_code = 10461
!Sample_contact_country = USA
!Sample_instrument_model = Illumina HiSeq 2500
!Sample_library_selection = other

!Sample_relation = SRA: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra?term=SRX15010697
